law: A LANE THAT NEEDS ART FILES A REQUEST. IT DOES NOT COOK IT AND IT DOES NOT BLOCK.
how_it_works: ANY lane files a request here the moment it hits missing art. It keeps building around it.
The ART lane picks requests up, cooks candidates, and Paolo thumbs them.
A request is CLOSED only when the art is MEASURED in the surface he plays -- not when it is cooked, not when it is approved. gates/art_request_gate.js checks the marker.
That closes the loop that failed seven times in one month: approved art sitting in banks/ while the game drew something else.

requests.what: THE DOG. A feral dog body, walkable, 8 facings, at the character ladder.
requests.why_paolo: "maybe I wanna fuck around and start putting, you know, dogs and and swarms of flies as, like, low tier, you know, biome level one enemies or something" (8/26). He named the dog FIRST. The bestiary research delivered 8/25 calls it the headline animal of Tier 1: "FERAL DOGS. The one the ecology literature lists first among vertebrate scavengers and the one every collapse account features. Not wolves. Somebody's pets, in a pack, ten years on. That is the most Bohemia enemy imaginable and it costs nothing in fiction."
requests.measured_gap: Measured, not estimated: the repository contains NO animal body art of any kind -- no dog, no coyote, no four-legged anything, in any bank. THE VALLEY HAS ANIMALS IN IT (8/26) shipped flies, rats and ravens because every one of those is a small dark moving MARK (specks, a dash, a silhouette) and needs no character sprite. A dog is a BODY. The 45 DEGREE ART LAW and REUSE-FIRST both say a lane does not invent creature pixels because it is in a hurry, so the mechanism shipped with the dog's row present and set to 0 in ANIMAL_DENSITY, held there by gates/the_valley_has_animals_gate.js.
requests.what_unblocks_it: One row of numbers in ANIMAL_DENSITY and a draw branch beside the raven's. The placement rule, the determinism, the beat movement, the by-district density and the performance cap are all built and gated already. When the art lands the dog is one line.
requests.notes: 45 DEGREE ART LAW applies: seen from the world's three-quarter view like everything else, never flat side-on. A PACK is Tier 2 (pack AI, flanking, breaking off and coming back) and is where the RF4 movement work lands -- but a single dog is Tier 1 and is enough to start. RESERVED AND NOT MINE: whether a dog is ever hostile, and what a den contains, are his.
spec: A FERAL DOG, three-quarter 45 view like everything else in the world (45 DEGREE ART LAW) -- never flat side-on. Standing and walking, on the same pixel ladder the human bodies use so it scales through the same zoom stops without a fractional blit.
8 FACINGS, the same compass the player and the cast use (N NE E SE S SW W NW), so pplFace/dirOf can drive it with no new mapping.

SOMEBODY'S PET, TEN YEARS ON. The research is explicit that these are NOT wolves: shepherds, retrievers, pit mixes, the dogs a city actually had. Ribs showing, coat matted and sun-bleached, a collar on some of them -- the collar is the whole story and costs one row of pixels.

READS AT A GLANCE AT THE SMALL STOPS. It shares a screen with rats (a 2px dash) and ravens (a small silhouette); a dog has to be unmistakably bigger and four-legged at the 44px cell, or Tier 1 becomes a smear.
PALETTE: the world's own desert-washed range, no new hues. PURPLE RESERVATION applies -- purple belongs to the Amalgamation alone.
